assumptions: material:material:bench-t3: Poisson ratio derived as E/(2G) - 1 = 0.29 (E = 210000 MPa, G = 81395.34884 MPa)

Profile caepipe-mbf-si-pilot-1: MBF version 15.10, OPTIONS SI with the default vertical axis Y; SWBPIPE global X, Y, Z are written unchanged as the target program's X, Y, Z, with gravity along -Y. The writer always writes Y vertical: SWBPIPE has one vertical convention (weight along -Y) and the model document records no vertical axis, so a Z-vertical import, which arrives rotated, is written Y-vertical.

Lengths are written in mm, forces in N, moments in N*m, modulus in N/mm2 (= MPa), temperatures in C; SI source units scale to these by an exact power of ten, and US-customary units by the exact definitions listed in MBF-SI-UNITS-NORMALIZED (Design caepipe-mbf-import.md section 5.2).
Load case mapping: mechanical cases (concentrated force, concentrated moment, weight) -> 'Sustained (W+P)'; thermal and imposed-displacement cases -> 'Expansion (T1)'.
Materials are written temperature-independent: identical E and expansion coefficient at 20 C, 170 C; the optional allowable, yield and rupture columns are omitted.

Every LOADS entry has Pressure 1 = 0 and specific gravity 0 (empty pipe); Temperature 1 = reference temperature + the element's SWBPIPE thermal change (summed when several primitives act on one element).

Piping code B311-80, chosen by the caller, is written in OPTIONS; OPCODE is written 0,0,0: axial force in the code stress off and liberal allowable off (code-stress settings only), and B31J off, so SIFs and flexibility factors come from the code's own appendix and a tee assembles no branch flexibility (Analysis; Format of .MBF, OPCODE). Every bend carries the user flexibility factor, which replaces the code's value (Bend).

Each curved bend (curved_bend_macro_element) is written as one layout row at the tangent intersection (TI) of its adjacent straights: 'T<n>,KI,B<radius mm>,<offsets to the TI>' with the user flexibility factor as the comment 'FF=<k>'; the incoming straight pipe and the bend share that row and its properties. The target program reports the near and far tangent points as nodes '<n>A' and '<n>B', which node_map assigns to the SWBPIPE tangent-point nodes; the next row's offsets start at the TI. The single user factor stands for SWBPIPE's in-plane and out-of-plane bending factor alike.
Model members the SWBPIPE solve does not read (analysis_status, data_boundary, diagnostics, lines, unresolved_assumptions, constraints, equipment_interfaces, rule_pack_refs) are not exported.
